ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=kx+b$ intersects the line $y=mx+n$ at point $C(1, 5)$. What is the solution set for the inequality $mx+n<kx+b$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the graph, we can see that to the left of point C, the line $y=mx+n$ is above the line $y=kx+b$, and to the right of point C, the line $y=mx+n$ is below the line $y=kx+b$,\\
$\because$ The line $y=kx+b$ intersects the line $y=mx+n$ at point C(1, 5),\\
$\therefore$ The solution set of the inequality $mx+n<kx+b$ is $\boxed{x>1}$.
